UNITY-GLOBHEALTH-2025.name: Global Health Unity
UNITY-GLOBHEALTH-2025.description: International collaborative network for global health initiatives

UNITY-FINTECH-2025.name: FinTech Alliance
UNITY-FINTECH-2025.description: Collaborative network for financial technology innovation, digital banking transformation, and regulatory harmonization across global markets

WHO-001.name: WHO
WHO-001.description: The World Health Organization is the United Nations specialized agency for international public health. Established in 1948, WHO leads and coordinates the international health response, sets global health standards, and provides technical assistance to member states across 194 countries. WHO operates through six regional offices and country offices in over 150 nations, addressing infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, mental health, environmental health, and health systems strengthening. The organization plays a central convening role in global health governance and emergency preparedness.
WHO-001.duty: WHO is responsible for providing leadership on global health matters, shaping the health research agenda, setting norms and standards, articulating evidence-based policy options, providing technical support to countries, and monitoring and assessing health trends. During health emergencies, WHO coordinates international response efforts, deploys emergency medical teams, and manages the Health Emergency Preparedness and Response framework.
WHO-001.fundingSource: Member state contributions (20%), voluntary donations from governments and foundations (80%)

UNICEF-001.name: UNICEF
UNICEF-001.description: UNICEF is the United Nations agency responsible for providing humanitarian and developmental aid to children worldwide. Present in over 190 countries and territories, UNICEF is the world's largest single vaccine buyer, procuring more than 2 billion doses annually for routine immunization and outbreak response on behalf of nearly 100 countries. The organization works across health, nutrition, education, water and sanitation, child protection, and social inclusion. UNICEF operates on the front lines of humanitarian crises and also drives long-term development programs to ensure every child survives and thrives.
UNICEF-001.duty: UNICEF is mandated to advocate for the protection of children's rights, to help meet their basic needs, and to expand their opportunities to reach their full potential. This includes delivering vaccines and essential medicines to children in conflict and disaster zones, running nutrition programs for acutely malnourished children, providing access to clean water and sanitation in underserved communities, and supporting governments in building child-responsive social protection systems.
UNICEF-001.fundingSource: Voluntary contributions from governments (70%), private sector partnerships (20%), individual donations (10%)

REDC-001.name: Red Cross
REDC-001.fullName: International Committee of the Red Cross
REDC-001.description: The International Committee of the Red Cross is an impartial, neutral, and independent humanitarian organization whose exclusively humanitarian mission is to protect the lives and dignity of victims of armed conflict and other situations of violence, and to provide them with assistance. Founded in 1863 in Geneva, the ICRC is the founding body of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and operates in over 100 countries. It is internationally recognized under the Geneva Conventions as a guardian of international humanitarian law.
REDC-001.duty: The ICRC's primary responsibilities include visiting prisoners of war and civilian detainees, tracing missing persons, reuniting separated families, and providing medical assistance in conflict zones. The organization operates field hospitals, trauma care units, and physical rehabilitation centers in war-affected areas. It also works to promote and strengthen international humanitarian law, training armed forces and providing legal advisory services to governments.
REDC-001.fundingSource: Government donations (65%), public fundraising (25%), corporate partnerships (10%)

MSF-001.name: MSF
MSF-001.description: Médecins Sans Frontières, known internationally as Doctors Without Borders, is an international humanitarian organization that provides medical care to people affected by conflict, epidemics, disasters, or exclusion from healthcare. MSF operates in over 70 countries with more than 65,000 staff, the majority of whom are locally hired. The organization is known for its independence, impartiality, and willingness to operate in the most dangerous and challenging environments, including active conflict zones. MSF also engages in advocacy and campaigns to improve access to essential medicines worldwide.
MSF-001.duty: MSF delivers emergency medical care in conflict zones, epidemic response including cholera, Ebola, and measles outbreaks, surgical care for war-wounded patients, treatment for malnutrition and neglected tropical diseases, mental health support in crisis settings, and sexual and reproductive health services. MSF also campaigns publicly for access to affordable medicines and vaccines, particularly for neglected diseases affecting low-income populations.

CDC-001.name: CDC
CDC-001.fullName: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
CDC-001.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is the national public health agency of the United States, operating under the Department of Health and Human Services. CDC is one of the world's leading public health institutes, employing more than 10,000 employees and with a global presence through the Global Disease Detection program operating in over 60 countries. The agency is internationally recognized for its expertise in epidemiology, laboratory science, and public health practice, and plays a key role in global health security through the Global Health Security Agenda.
CDC-001.duty: CDC is responsible for protecting public health and safety through the control and prevention of disease, injury, and disability. Its global mandate includes detecting and responding to new and emerging health threats, implementing disease surveillance systems, building laboratory capacity in partner countries, training epidemiologists through the Field Epidemiology Training Program, and supporting health system strengthening in low and middle-income countries. CDC also leads the US government's response to international public health emergencies.
CDC-001.fundingSource: Federal government appropriations (85%), user fees and reimbursements (15%)

GAVI-001.name: GAVI
GAVI-001.fullName: Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization
GAVI-001.description: Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, is a public-private global health partnership committed to increasing access to immunization in poor countries. Since its creation in 2000, Gavi has contributed to the immunization of more than 1 billion children and the prevention of over 17 million future deaths. The Alliance brings together developing country and donor governments, WHO, UNICEF, the World Bank, the vaccine industry, research and technical agencies, civil society, and the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. Gavi uses innovative finance mechanisms to secure sustainable funding and adequate supply of quality vaccines.
GAVI-001.duty: Gavi's primary responsibilities include co-financing vaccines for eligible low-income countries, supporting the introduction of new and underused vaccines, strengthening health and immunization systems, and shaping vaccine markets to make them more accessible and affordable. Gavi also manages the COVAX Facility alongside WHO and CEPI, working to ensure equitable global access to COVID-19 vaccines and future pandemic vaccines.
GAVI-001.fundingSource: Donor governments (60%), Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (20%), private sector (10%), innovative financing (10%)

WBANK-001.name: World Bank
WBANK-001.description: The World Bank Group is one of the world's largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries. It consists of five institutions: the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Development Association, the International Finance Corporation, the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, and the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes. In the health sector, the World Bank is the largest external funder of health systems in developing countries, investing approximately $4 billion annually in health projects. The Bank plays a critical role in health financing, health system reform, and pandemic preparedness.
WBANK-001.duty: The World Bank's health mandate focuses on helping countries build strong, resilient, and equitable health systems. This includes financing health infrastructure, supporting universal health coverage initiatives, strengthening health workforce capacity, improving health data systems, and funding disease control programs. The Bank also leads the Health Emergency Preparedness and Response Trust Fund, which supports countries in building capacities to prevent, detect, and respond to health emergencies.
WBANK-001.fundingSource: Bond issuances in capital markets (70%), member country subscriptions (20%), loan repayments (10%)

GATES-001.name: Gates Foundation
GATES-001.description: The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation is the world's largest private charitable foundation, with an endowment of approximately $70 billion. Founded in 2000 by Bill and Melinda Gates, the foundation works to reduce extreme poverty and improve healthcare worldwide. In global health, the foundation has committed over $50 billion since its inception, funding vaccine development, malaria elimination, HIV prevention, tuberculosis treatment, and agricultural innovation in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. The foundation operates through strategic partnerships with multilateral organizations, governments, and research institutions.
GATES-001.duty: The Gates Foundation's global health program focuses on developing and delivering tools — vaccines, drugs, and diagnostics — needed to reduce the burden of infectious diseases disproportionately affecting the world's poorest populations. The foundation funds research and development for neglected diseases, supports large-scale vaccine immunization programs through Gavi, backs malaria control efforts, funds contraceptive research and reproductive health programs, and invests in strengthening health systems across sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
GATES-001.fundingSource: Endowment from Bill and Melinda Gates (95%), Warren Buffett contributions (5%)

HARV-001.name: Harvard
HARV-001.description: Harvard University is a private Ivy League research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and home to the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, one of the world's leading institutions for public health research and education. Harvard's global health programs span epidemiology, biostatistics, health policy, environmental health, and global health delivery. The university has active research programs in over 40 countries and trains thousands of global health professionals annually through its graduate programs. Harvard researchers have made foundational contributions to understanding HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, and non-communicable diseases.
HARV-001.duty: Harvard's contributions to global health include conducting cutting-edge epidemiological and clinical research, developing evidence-based health policies, training the next generation of global health leaders, and providing technical assistance to ministries of health in low and middle-income countries. The Harvard Global Health Institute facilitates interdisciplinary research collaboration across the university's schools, including Medicine, Public Health, Business, Law, and Government, to address complex global health challenges.
HARV-001.fundingSource: Endowment returns (35%), research grants (30%), tuition and fees (20%), donations (15%)

OXFD-001.name: Oxford
OXFD-001.description: The University of Oxford is a collegiate research university in Oxford, England, and one of the world's leading centers for global health research. Oxford's Nuffield Department of Medicine, the Jenner Institute, and the Oxford Vaccine Group have been at the forefront of vaccine development for decades, most notably co-developing the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. Oxford has active research partnerships across Africa and Asia through programs such as the Oxford University Clinical Research Unit and the African Oxford Health. The university's researchers have contributed seminal work on malaria, HIV, tuberculosis, and emerging infectious diseases.
OXFD-001.duty: Oxford's global health responsibilities include conducting large-scale clinical trials for vaccines and therapeutics, building research capacity in low and middle-income countries through long-term partnerships, training clinicians and researchers in field epidemiology and clinical research methodology, and translating scientific discoveries into practical health interventions. Oxford also engages in health policy analysis and advocacy, advising governments and international organizations on evidence-based approaches to disease control and health system strengthening.
OXFD-001.fundingSource: Research grants (40%), endowment and investments (25%), tuition fees (20%), government funding (15%)

PAHO-001.name: PAHO
PAHO-001.description: The Pan American Health Organization is the specialized international health agency for the Americas, serving as the WHO Regional Office for the Americas. Established in 1902, PAHO is the world's oldest international public health agency, working with countries to improve and protect people's health across 35 member states. PAHO addresses communicable and non-communicable diseases, environmental health, health systems strengthening, and health emergencies across Latin America and the Caribbean.
PAHO-001.duty: PAHO provides technical cooperation to countries across the Americas to strengthen health systems, prevent and control disease, and improve health equity. It coordinates regional responses to health emergencies, sets regional health standards, trains health professionals, and facilitates evidence-based policy development across member states.
PAHO-001.fundingSource: Member state contributions (55%), WHO core budget (25%), voluntary contributions (20%)

UNITAID-001.name: Unitaid
UNITAID-001.description: Unitaid is an international organization that invests in innovations to prevent, diagnose, and treat HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria more quickly, affordably, and effectively. Hosted by WHO in Geneva, Unitaid works by identifying bottlenecks in the availability and affordability of health products and catalyzing market changes to overcome them. Its innovative financing model, primarily funded through a solidarity levy on airline tickets, enables it to take strategic market interventions that unlock access to health commodities at scale.
UNITAID-001.duty: Unitaid's mandate is to contribute to scaling up access to better health products for HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria in low-income countries. It does this through strategic market interventions including negotiating reduced prices, supporting product registration, funding product development, and de-risking early market entry for essential medicines and diagnostics.
UNITAID-001.fundingSource: Airline solidarity levy (70%), direct government contributions (30%)

AFDB-001.name: AfDB
AFDB-001.description: The African Development Bank is a multilateral development finance institution established to spur sustainable economic development and social progress in Africa. With 81 member states including 54 African countries, the Bank finances transformative projects across infrastructure, agriculture, industry, and social sectors. In health, AfDB focuses on health system strengthening, pandemic preparedness infrastructure, and financing universal health coverage initiatives across the continent.
AFDB-001.duty: AfDB provides loans, grants, and technical assistance to African governments and private sector entities for health infrastructure development, disease control programs, and health system reform. The Bank co-finances health projects with partners including WHO, World Bank, and bilateral donors, and plays a key role in mobilizing domestic and international resources for African health priorities.
AFDB-001.fundingSource: Member country subscriptions (60%), bond issuances (30%), retained earnings (10%)

LSHTM-001.name: LSHTM
LSHTM-001.fullName: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine
LSHTM-001.description: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is a world-leading public health research institution and postgraduate university. LSHTM is consistently ranked among the top schools of public health globally, conducting research on infectious diseases, global health policy, epidemiology, and health systems. The School has particular expertise in tropical medicine, malaria, HIV, tuberculosis, neglected tropical diseases, and humanitarian health. LSHTM trains over 4,000 students annually from more than 150 countries.
LSHTM-001.duty: LSHTM conducts high-impact research that informs global health policy and practice, trains the next generation of global health professionals, and provides expert advice to governments and international organizations. The School leads major research consortia on malaria vaccine development, tuberculosis diagnostics, and health system strengthening in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
LSHTM-001.fundingSource: Research grants (55%), tuition fees (25%), government funding (15%), donations (5%)

IAVI-001.name: IAVI
IAVI-001.description: The International AIDS Vaccine Initiative is a global nonprofit scientific organization working to accelerate the development of vaccines and other biomedical interventions to end the AIDS epidemic. Founded in 1996, IAVI conducts basic science research, clinical trials, and product development for HIV vaccines and broadly neutralizing antibodies. IAVI also applies its platform technologies to other emerging infectious diseases and works to ensure that vaccines reach people in the countries most affected by HIV.
IAVI-001.duty: IAVI's primary responsibilities include conducting HIV vaccine research and clinical trials in partnership with academic and industry collaborators, building clinical trial capacity in Africa and India, advocating for increased investment in HIV vaccine development, and ensuring that successful HIV vaccines are accessible to low-income countries through advance market commitments and technology transfer.
IAVI-001.fundingSource: US government (45%), Gates Foundation (25%), European governments (20%), other donors (10%)

JPM-001.name: JPMorgan
JPM-001.description: JPMorgan Chase is the largest bank in the United States and one of the world's most prominent financial services firms, with assets exceeding $3.7 trillion. The firm operates across investment banking, commercial banking, asset management, and consumer finance. JPMorgan has invested heavily in fintech innovation, operating one of the largest technology budgets in financial services at over $15 billion annually.
JPM-001.duty: JPMorgan leads in developing enterprise blockchain solutions, real-time payment infrastructure, and AI-driven risk management systems. The firm's Onyx division operates JPM Coin for institutional payments and has pioneered tokenized deposit platforms for cross-border settlement.

STRIPE-001.name: Stripe
STRIPE-001.description: Stripe is a global technology company that builds economic infrastructure for the internet. Processing hundreds of billions of dollars annually, Stripe's payment platform powers millions of businesses from startups to Fortune 500 companies across 46 countries. The company has expanded beyond payments into business incorporation, treasury management, and financial data analytics.
STRIPE-001.duty: Stripe develops and maintains payment processing APIs, fraud prevention tools, and financial infrastructure that enables businesses to accept payments, manage revenue, and expand globally. Stripe also operates Stripe Atlas for business incorporation and Stripe Treasury for embedded banking services.

REVOLUT-001.name: Revolut
REVOLUT-001.description: Revolut is a global neobank and financial technology company offering banking, crypto trading, stock trading, and international money transfers to over 40 million customers worldwide. Founded in London in 2015, Revolut has grown into one of Europe's most valuable fintech companies, holding banking licenses in multiple jurisdictions and continuously expanding its product suite.
REVOLUT-001.duty: Revolut provides digital-first banking services including multi-currency accounts, instant international transfers, cryptocurrency trading, and budgeting tools. The company focuses on eliminating hidden fees in cross-border transactions and making financial services accessible through its mobile platform.

FCA-001.name: FCA
FCA-001.description: The Financial Conduct Authority is the financial regulatory body in the United Kingdom, responsible for regulating over 50,000 financial services firms. The FCA has been a global pioneer in fintech regulation through its Regulatory Sandbox program, which allows innovative firms to test products in a controlled environment. The FCA's approach to regulation has been widely replicated internationally.
FCA-001.duty: The FCA regulates financial markets and firms, protects consumers, and promotes competition in financial services. In fintech, the FCA operates the Innovation Hub and Regulatory Sandbox, develops regulatory frameworks for emerging technologies including AI and crypto assets, and leads international regulatory cooperation through the Global Financial Innovation Network.

VISA-001.name: Visa
VISA-001.description: Visa is the world's leader in digital payments, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions, and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories. Visa's network processes over 250 billion transactions annually with a capacity to handle 65,000 transactions per second. The company has invested extensively in tokenization, real-time payments, and fraud prevention technologies.
VISA-001.duty: Visa operates the world's largest electronic payment network, enabling secure, reliable, and instant digital transactions globally. Visa develops payment security standards, fraud detection systems using AI, and new payment modalities including tap-to-pay, digital wallets, and B2B payment solutions.

CHAINALYSIS-001.name: Chainalysis
CHAINALYSIS-001.description: Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform providing compliance and investigation software to government agencies, financial institutions, and cryptocurrency businesses in over 70 countries. The company's tools map cryptocurrency transactions to real-world entities, enabling regulatory compliance, fraud detection, and law enforcement investigations across blockchain networks.
CHAINALYSIS-001.duty: Chainalysis provides blockchain analytics, compliance solutions, and investigation tools that help organizations understand and monitor cryptocurrency activity. The company works with regulators to develop evidence-based cryptocurrency policies and provides training to law enforcement agencies on blockchain forensics.

MPESA-001.name: M-Pesa
MPESA-001.description: M-Pesa is the world's most successful mobile money platform, serving over 50 million active users across seven African countries. Launched in Kenya in 2007 by Safaricom and Vodafone, M-Pesa has fundamentally transformed financial inclusion in East Africa, enabling millions of unbanked individuals to send money, pay bills, access credit, and save through their mobile phones.
MPESA-001.duty: M-Pesa operates mobile money infrastructure enabling peer-to-peer transfers, merchant payments, salary disbursements, and microfinance services. The platform serves as the backbone for digital financial services in East Africa and is expanding its super-app ecosystem to include savings, insurance, and investment products.

MITSLOAN-001.name: MIT Sloan
MITSLOAN-001.description: MIT Sloan School of Management is one of the world's leading business schools, with pioneering research programs in financial technology, digital currencies, and AI applications in finance. The MIT Digital Currency Initiative and the MIT Laboratory for Financial Engineering have produced influential research on blockchain technology, central bank digital currencies, and algorithmic trading systems.
MITSLOAN-001.duty: MIT Sloan conducts foundational research in financial technology, trains future fintech leaders, and provides independent analysis of emerging financial technologies. The school's research directly informs regulatory policy on digital currencies, algorithmic trading, and AI governance in financial services.

BIS-001.name: BIS
BIS-001.description: The Bank for International Settlements is an international financial institution owned by 63 central banks, serving as a bank for central banks. The BIS Innovation Hub drives fintech innovation in central banking, with projects on central bank digital currencies, tokenized assets, and cross-border payment systems. The BIS plays a critical role in setting global financial standards and facilitating international monetary cooperation.
BIS-001.duty: The BIS provides banking services to central banks, conducts research on financial stability and monetary policy, and sets global standards for banking supervision through the Basel Committee. The BIS Innovation Hub experiments with emerging technologies to improve the functioning of the global financial system.

ANTGROUP-001.name: Ant Group
ANTGROUP-001.description: Ant Group is one of the world's largest fintech companies, operating Alipay — a digital payment platform serving over 1.3 billion users globally. The company provides digital payment services, wealth management, insurance, credit services, and blockchain solutions. Ant Group's technology stack processes over 100,000 transactions per second and has pioneered AI-driven credit scoring for underserved populations.
ANTGROUP-001.duty: Ant Group develops and operates digital payment infrastructure, AI-powered financial services, and blockchain platforms. The company focuses on using technology to make financial services more inclusive, efficient, and accessible, particularly for small businesses and underbanked populations across Asia and emerging markets.

MEET-001.title: Global Health Summit 2025
MEET-001.purpose: The summit was convened to establish unified global health priorities for 2025-2030, with a specific focus on accelerating vaccination coverage in sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia. WHO, UNICEF, and GAVI sought to align their strategic frameworks following the post-COVID recovery period, addressing supply chain vulnerabilities exposed during the pandemic and setting measurable targets for immunization equity. The meeting also aimed to define clear roles and responsibilities among the three organizations to avoid duplication of effort and maximize resource utilization.
MEET-001.outcome: The three organizations agreed on an accelerated vaccine distribution framework targeting 50 low-income countries by Q2 2026, with GAVI leading procurement, UNICEF managing last-mile delivery logistics, and WHO providing technical oversight and quality assurance. A joint monitoring committee was established with quarterly reporting obligations. The summit also produced a consensus document on cold chain infrastructure investment priorities, committing a combined $180 million over three years to expand refrigerated storage capacity in 20 high-burden countries. WHO agreed to lead a technical working group on vaccine hesitancy, developing culturally adapted communication strategies for deployment through UNICEF's country office network.

MEET-002.title: Disease Prevention and Outbreak Response Workshop
MEET-002.purpose: This workshop was organized in response to a series of cholera outbreaks across the Horn of Africa and flooding-related disease spikes in South Asia. WHO, MSF, and CDC convened to share real-time epidemiological data, assess the adequacy of existing outbreak response protocols, and identify systemic gaps in the early warning and response architecture. The meeting also sought to evaluate the effectiveness of the International Health Regulations framework in triggering timely coordinated responses and to propose concrete improvements based on lessons from recent field operations.
MEET-002.outcome: The three organizations developed a unified early warning system protocol integrating WHO's Global Outbreak Alert and Response Network with CDC's Emergency Operations Center real-time monitoring feeds and MSF's field intelligence reporting. The new system enables cross-organizational data sharing within 24 hours of a confirmed outbreak threshold being reached. A joint rapid response roster of 150 pre-credentialed field epidemiologists, drawn equally from all three organizations, was established for immediate deployment. CDC committed to hosting a biannual simulation exercise to test response coordination under the new framework, with the first exercise scheduled for February 2026.

MEET-003.title: Humanitarian Aid Coordination Conference
MEET-003.purpose: Following simultaneous humanitarian crises in Sudan, Myanmar, and Haiti, UNICEF, Red Cross, and the Gates Foundation convened to review the adequacy of existing coordination mechanisms and resource allocation procedures. The conference addressed the persistent challenge of funding fragmentation in humanitarian response, where multiple organizations raise separate appeals for the same crisis, leading to donor fatigue and inefficient resource deployment. The meeting also examined the role of private philanthropy in bridging funding gaps left by strained government humanitarian budgets.
MEET-003.outcome: The three organizations established a joint rapid response fund of $75 million, with Gates Foundation providing $40 million, UNICEF contributing $20 million, and Red Cross allocating $15 million. A unified humanitarian appeal template was adopted to consolidate funding requests and reduce donor fatigue. A joint logistics hub was agreed upon for East Africa, co-managed by UNICEF and Red Cross, with the Gates Foundation funding the infrastructure build-out over 18 months. The organizations also agreed to a data-sharing protocol for real-time beneficiary tracking, enabling better coordination of aid delivery and preventing duplication in service provision.

MEET-004.title: Field Hospital Standards and Emergency Protocol Review
MEET-004.purpose: Red Cross and MSF convened a bilateral technical meeting to review and harmonize their respective field hospital standards and emergency medical protocols. Both organizations had identified inconsistencies in triage procedures, surgical protocols, and post-operative care standards that complicated patient handover in shared operational areas, particularly in Yemen, Democratic Republic of Congo, and Syria. The meeting aimed to produce a joint clinical governance framework applicable in complex emergencies where both organizations operate simultaneously.
MEET-004.outcome: A standardized emergency medical protocol for field hospitals in high-risk conflict environments was produced, covering triage classification, essential surgical procedures, infection prevention and control, and post-operative care standards. The protocol was validated against WHO's Emergency Medical Teams minimum standards and is designed for immediate field deployment. Both organizations committed to joint training exercises twice per year, and a shared medical supply stockpile framework was agreed upon to reduce procurement duplication in co-located operations. The document will be submitted to the WHO Emergency Medical Teams initiative for endorsement as an international field standard.

MEET-005.title: Vaccine Cold Chain Infrastructure Investment Forum
MEET-005.purpose: WHO, UNICEF, CDC, and GAVI convened to address a critical bottleneck in global immunization programs — the inadequacy of cold chain infrastructure in remote and underserved regions. Temperature-sensitive vaccines, including rotavirus, pneumococcal, and HPV vaccines, were being wasted at rates of up to 30% in several high-burden countries due to unreliable refrigeration. The forum sought to develop a coordinated investment strategy combining capital financing, technology innovation, and capacity building to create a resilient cold chain network aligned with the Immunization Agenda 2030.
MEET-005.outcome: A $120 million investment package was approved for cold chain infrastructure across 35 countries, with GAVI committing $60 million, UNICEF $30 million, and CDC providing technical assistance valued at $15 million, with the remainder from bilateral donor contributions channeled through WHO. A technology working group was established to evaluate and endorse solar-powered refrigeration units for deployment in off-grid communities. UNICEF agreed to lead procurement of 15,000 new cold chain units by end of 2026. WHO committed to updating its cold chain equipment performance qualification and testing norms. CDC will provide supply chain management training to national immunization program staff in 15 priority countries.

MEET-006.title: Post-Pandemic Public Health Policy Reform Consultation
MEET-006.purpose: WHO, CDC, and Harvard University convened a high-level policy consultation to systematically review public health policies that were stress-tested during the COVID-19 pandemic. The consultation focused on four domains: International Health Regulations reform, national pandemic preparedness legislation, health system resilience frameworks, and global health financing mechanisms. The objective was to produce an evidence-based policy reform agenda drawing on academic research, regulatory experience, and operational field data.
MEET-006.outcome: The consultation produced a comprehensive policy reform document containing 12 priority recommendations covering amendments to the International Health Regulations to strengthen compliance mechanisms, establishment of national pandemic preparedness funds with mandatory minimum reserves, reform of WHO's emergency financing architecture to enable faster resource mobilization, and creation of a global health security index with binding reporting obligations for member states. Harvard agreed to lead a multi-year research program to evaluate the implementation of these recommendations. WHO will present the reform agenda to the World Health Assembly in May 2026. CDC committed to advocating for the reforms through bilateral diplomatic channels with G20 health ministers.

MEET-007.title: Humanitarian Crisis Management Capacity Building Program
MEET-007.purpose: UNICEF, Red Cross, and MSF jointly organized an advanced crisis management training program for frontline humanitarian staff in East Africa. The program was designed in response to a documented skills gap identified across all three organizations in managing complex, multi-hazard emergencies involving simultaneous conflict, disease outbreak, and climate-related displacement. The training focused on integrated emergency coordination, inter-agency communication protocols, psychological first aid, and community engagement in hostile environments.
MEET-007.outcome: A total of 250 humanitarian personnel from across UNICEF, Red Cross, and MSF field offices in Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, and Ethiopia were certified in advanced crisis management. The training curriculum, developed jointly over six months, was formally adopted as the standard humanitarian response training framework for all three organizations operating in East Africa. A community of practice was established among certified trainers to ensure ongoing knowledge exchange. The three organizations agreed to co-facilitate two follow-up refresher training sessions per year and to develop a digital learning platform to extend training access to staff in remote field locations.

MEET-008.title: Global Health Data Governance and Sharing Framework Negotiation
MEET-008.purpose: WHO, MSF, Harvard, and Oxford University convened to negotiate a legally binding framework for the secure sharing of health data across international research and operational organizations. The meeting addressed growing concerns about data sovereignty, patient privacy, and the asymmetric benefits of data sharing between high-income research institutions and low-income country partners. The framework was intended to establish clear data governance principles, access conditions, and benefit-sharing mechanisms that would enable real-time health surveillance while protecting individual and national data rights.
MEET-008.outcome: A comprehensive health data governance framework was signed, enabling real-time sharing of de-identified health surveillance data across 40 participating nations. The framework establishes a tiered data access model with open access for aggregated public health indicators, restricted access for individual-level research data, and a joint data ethics committee with rotating membership from all signatory organizations. Harvard and Oxford agreed to provide data science capacity building support to health ministries in 15 low-income countries to enable meaningful participation in the framework. MSF negotiated inclusion of a humanitarian exemption clause enabling emergency data sharing within 6 hours of a declared outbreak. WHO will serve as the framework secretariat and annual reporting body.

MEET-009.title: East Africa Flood Disaster Relief Coordination Summit
MEET-009.purpose: Following catastrophic flooding across Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda that displaced over 2 million people and triggered outbreaks of cholera and malaria, Red Cross, UNICEF, and the Gates Foundation convened an emergency coordination summit to align relief operations, prevent duplication, and rapidly mobilize resources. The summit sought to establish a unified incident command structure for the multi-country response and to agree on a division of operational responsibilities that leveraged each organization's comparative strengths.
MEET-009.outcome: A coordinated relief operation was deployed to 15 affected regions across the three countries, with Red Cross leading search and rescue and medical care, UNICEF managing water, sanitation, and nutrition responses, and the Gates Foundation providing emergency financing of $25 million to cover immediate gaps. A joint logistics system was established, achieving a 30% reduction in transport costs through consolidated supply chains. A cholera vaccination campaign was launched within 72 hours, targeting 800,000 people in highest-risk areas. The Gates Foundation committed an additional $15 million for early recovery programming focused on rebuilding health infrastructure and restoring livelihoods in the most severely affected communities.

MEET-010.title: Annual Global Health Unity Conference 2026
MEET-010.purpose: The annual conference brought together the five core operational members of the Global Health Unity to review collective performance against 2025 targets, present updated global health burden data, and set strategic priorities for 2026. The conference focused particularly on three emerging challenges: antimicrobial resistance, the growing burden of non-communicable diseases in low-income countries, and the financing gap for health system strengthening in fragile states. It also served as the formal accountability forum for all joint programs initiated in previous meetings.
MEET-010.outcome: A comprehensive performance review confirmed achievement of 78% of 2025 joint targets, with vaccination coverage improvements in 42 of 50 target countries. The conference set ambitious 2026 targets including a 15% reduction in under-5 child mortality across Unity member countries' operational areas, a 20% increase in vaccination coverage in the lowest quartile of performing countries, and the launch of a joint antimicrobial resistance surveillance network. A new joint working group on non-communicable diseases was established, led by WHO with CDC co-chairing. The conference also approved a collective advocacy position on climate change and health to be presented at COP31.

MEET-011.title: Health Literacy and Community Education Program Development
MEET-011.purpose: Harvard, Oxford, and WHO convened to design and launch a coordinated program of health literacy interventions targeting underserved communities in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Research from both universities had identified a persistent gap between the availability of health services and their utilization, driven significantly by low health literacy, cultural barriers, and misinformation. The meeting sought to combine Harvard's behavioral science expertise, Oxford's community health worker research, and WHO's normative guidance to produce an evidence-based, scalable health education model.
MEET-011.outcome: Ten pilot health education programs were launched across six countries, each integrating community health worker training, school-based health curricula, and digital health literacy tools adapted for low-literacy populations. Harvard will lead program evaluation using a randomized controlled trial design across four sites, while Oxford manages implementation research in two additional sites. WHO committed to developing a global health literacy framework based on program findings, to be published by end of 2026. A joint academic paper on health literacy measurement methodologies was commissioned, with submission to The Lancet planned for Q3 2026. The programs collectively target reaching 500,000 community members in the first year.

MEET-012.title: Innovative Health Financing Mechanisms Forum
MEET-012.purpose: The World Bank, Gates Foundation, and GAVI convened a high-level forum to explore innovative financing mechanisms capable of addressing the estimated $176 billion annual gap in global health financing for low-income countries. Traditional donor aid flows had plateaued, and new approaches were needed to mobilize private capital, improve aid efficiency, and create sustainable domestic health financing systems. The forum specifically examined outcomes-based financing, health impact bonds, vaccine market shaping, and diaspora health investment vehicles.
MEET-012.outcome: Three innovative financing instruments were approved for immediate development and testing: a Global Health Impact Bond piloting outcomes-based payments for malaria and tuberculosis treatment in three African countries, a Vaccine Market Shaping Facility to accelerate price reductions for priority vaccines through advanced market commitments, and a Diaspora Health Investment Fund enabling overseas communities to channel remittances toward health infrastructure in their countries of origin. Combined, these instruments are projected to mobilize $200 million in new health financing within 24 months. The World Bank agreed to provide technical secretariat support, the Gates Foundation committed $50 million in catalytic financing, and GAVI will integrate the vaccine instrument into its financing architecture.

MEET-013.title: Infectious Disease Treatment Innovation Research Consortium Launch
MEET-013.purpose: Harvard, Oxford, and MSF convened to formally launch a multi-institution research consortium focused on developing and validating new treatment protocols for drug-resistant tuberculosis, severe malaria, and post-Ebola syndrome. MSF's operational experience had identified critical clinical management gaps for these conditions in field settings, while both universities had promising pre-clinical and early clinical research pipelines that required operational validation. The meeting aimed to establish the governance structure, research agenda, and funding architecture for the consortium.
MEET-013.outcome: Five joint research projects were formally initiated, covering a Phase II clinical trial of a novel drug-resistant tuberculosis regimen, a field validation study of simplified severe malaria treatment protocols for community health workers, a longitudinal cohort study on post-Ebola syndrome management, a health economic analysis of treatment protocol adoption incentives, and a systematic review of antimicrobial resistance drivers in humanitarian settings. A consortium governance board was established with rotating leadership between the three institutions. MSF committed to providing field sites and patient cohorts across six countries. Harvard and Oxford will co-lead the clinical research agenda. A joint grant application to the Wellcome Trust for £15 million was submitted to fund the program over five years.

MEET-014.title: Sustainable Global Health Financing Architecture Reform
MEET-014.purpose: The World Bank, WHO, and the Gates Foundation convened to address structural weaknesses in the global health financing architecture that had been exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent economic shocks. The meeting focused specifically on three interconnected challenges: the pro-cyclical nature of health aid that shrinks precisely when health needs expand during crises, the fragmentation of global health financing across hundreds of vertical funds with high transaction costs, and the inadequate capitalization of the WHO Contingency Fund for Emergencies relative to the scale of health emergencies.
MEET-014.outcome: An innovative financing mechanism was approved that will generate an estimated $500 million over five years through a combination of a sovereign health bond issuance facility managed by the World Bank, a pandemic insurance premium pool co-underwritten by the Gates Foundation, and a WHO emergency reserve replenishment mechanism linked to member state GDP growth. The World Bank will establish a new health financing trust fund to consolidate 12 existing fragmented funds, reducing administrative overhead by an estimated 18%. WHO agreed to reform its emergency financing procedures to enable resource mobilization within 72 hours of declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. The Gates Foundation committed to matching member state contributions to the WHO Contingency Fund dollar-for-dollar up to $100 million.

MEET-015.title: Global Health Security Emergency Preparedness Simulation Exercise
MEET-015.purpose: CDC, Red Cross, and UNICEF conducted a large-scale emergency preparedness simulation exercise designed to test inter-agency coordination under a realistic multi-country disease outbreak scenario. The exercise, code-named Operation Swift Shield, simulated a novel respiratory pathogen with pandemic potential emerging simultaneously in three regions. The objective was to identify coordination gaps, test updated communication protocols from the February 2026 simulation review, and certify health workers in revised emergency response guidelines.
MEET-015.outcome: Five hundred healthcare workers and emergency responders from CDC, Red Cross, and UNICEF were certified under updated emergency response guidelines developed following the Operation Swift Shield exercise findings. The simulation identified four critical coordination bottlenecks that have been addressed through protocol amendments: unclear command authority during multi-agency responses, insufficient pre-positioning of personal protective equipment in tropical regions, absence of a joint media communications protocol, and gaps in inter-operability between agency logistics management systems. A joint after-action report was produced with 22 actionable recommendations, 15 of which were immediately implemented. The revised protocols will be integrated into the February 2027 Global Health Security Index assessment.

MEET-016.title: MSF Field Operations Strategic Review and Resource Reallocation
MEET-016.purpose: MSF initiated a strategic review of its field operations across the Middle East and Central Africa, inviting WHO and Red Cross as key operational partners to provide external perspective on resource allocation priorities. The review was triggered by a significant increase in operational complexity in Sudan and Gaza, where MSF teams were facing simultaneous challenges of active conflict, disease outbreaks, and severe supply chain disruptions. The meeting sought to identify opportunities for better burden-sharing between the three organizations and to agree on a coordinated operational plan for the next six months.

MEET-017.title: UNICEF Sub-Saharan Africa Child Health Initiative Launch
MEET-017.purpose: UNICEF convened WHO and the Gates Foundation to formally launch a five-year child health initiative targeting the six countries in sub-Saharan Africa with the highest under-5 mortality rates: Nigeria, Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania, Uganda, Niger, and Mali. The initiative represents a significant scale-up from UNICEF's current country programs, requiring technical guidance from WHO on clinical protocols and substantial philanthropic co-financing from the Gates Foundation alongside government and donor contributions.

MEET-018.title: Oxford-WHO Vaccine Research and Development Alignment Meeting
MEET-018.purpose: Oxford University and WHO convened a technical alignment meeting to synchronize Oxford's current vaccine research pipeline with WHO's priority pathogen list and product development roadmap. With Oxford's Jenner Institute having multiple candidates in early clinical development for Marburg virus, Lassa fever, and a universal influenza vaccine, the meeting sought to ensure WHO's regulatory and normative guidance was integrated into the development process from the earliest stages. MSF was included to provide operational perspective on field deployment requirements and end-user needs.

MEET-019.title: CDC-GAVI Outbreak Preparedness and Vaccine Stockpile Planning Session
MEET-019.purpose: CDC and GAVI convened with WHO participation to conduct strategic planning for outbreak preparedness vaccine stockpiling in the context of emerging biological threats. Recent intelligence from CDC's Global Disease Detection network had identified three priority pathogens with elevated pandemic risk profiles, and the session aimed to align CDC's epidemiological risk assessments with GAVI's vaccine procurement and stockpiling capacity. WHO was included to provide regulatory guidance on stockpile management and international deployment protocols.

MEET-020.title: Gates Foundation 2026 Global Health Investment Strategy Review
MEET-020.purpose: The Gates Foundation convened WHO and UNICEF for an annual investment strategy review to align the foundation's 2026-2028 global health grant portfolio with the operational priorities and technical guidance of its two largest multilateral partners. With the foundation's global health program budget exceeding $2 billion annually, the alignment meeting ensures that philanthropic investments complement rather than duplicate multilateral programming, and that foundation-funded innovations are designed for scale-up through WHO and UNICEF's global networks.

MEET-021.title: Latin America Regional Immunization Strategy Summit
MEET-021.purpose: PAHO, GAVI, and UNICEF convened to develop a coordinated immunization strategy for Latin America and the Caribbean, addressing persistently low vaccination coverage in several countries following COVID-19 disruptions. The summit focused on rebuilding routine immunization services, introducing new vaccines including HPV and rotavirus in remaining countries, and designing targeted outreach campaigns for underserved indigenous and Afro-descendant communities.
MEET-021.outcome: A five-year regional immunization strategy was endorsed by all three organizations, targeting 95% coverage for all routine vaccines across 35 countries by 2030. PAHO committed to providing technical assistance through its country offices, GAVI approved accelerated co-financing for 12 eligible countries, and UNICEF agreed to lead procurement and supply chain management. A regional vaccine hesitancy working group was established, chaired by PAHO with UNICEF secretariat support.

MEET-022.title: HIV Vaccine Clinical Trial Coordination Meeting
MEET-022.purpose: IAVI, LSHTM, and the Gates Foundation convened to coordinate ongoing HIV vaccine clinical trials across sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda. The meeting addressed protocol harmonization challenges, interim safety data review, and planning for Phase IIb efficacy trials anticipated for 2026. The Gates Foundation's involvement focused on ensuring adequate funding continuity and strategic alignment with the broader HIV vaccine development ecosystem.
MEET-022.outcome: A harmonized clinical trial protocol was adopted across all seven active trial sites, enabling pooled data analysis and reducing regulatory submission burden. LSHTM agreed to lead the statistical analysis plan for the combined dataset. IAVI committed to expanding trial capacity to two additional sites in Rwanda and Mozambique. The Gates Foundation approved a $45 million grant extension to fund the program through 2027, contingent on positive 18-month safety data.

MEET-023.title: Africa Health Infrastructure Financing Roundtable
MEET-023.purpose: AfDB, World Bank, and the Gates Foundation convened a high-level roundtable to coordinate financing for health infrastructure across sub-Saharan Africa, where a chronic underinvestment in primary healthcare facilities had been identified as a key barrier to universal health coverage. The roundtable examined opportunities for blended finance instruments combining concessional loans, grants, and private capital to accelerate hospital and clinic construction in rural areas.
MEET-023.outcome: A joint Africa Health Infrastructure Initiative was launched with a combined commitment of $2.5 billion over five years, with AfDB contributing $1.2 billion in concessional loans, World Bank providing $1 billion through IDA credits, and Gates Foundation committing $300 million in catalytic grants. A blended finance facility was established to attract an additional $500 million in private investment. The initiative targets construction or rehabilitation of 500 primary healthcare facilities and 50 district hospitals across 20 African countries.

MEET-024.title: Tropical Disease Research Collaboration Workshop
MEET-024.purpose: LSHTM, MSF, and Oxford University convened to develop a joint research agenda for neglected tropical diseases including leishmaniasis, sleeping sickness, and Chagas disease. Despite affecting over one billion people globally, these diseases remain severely underfunded relative to their disease burden. The workshop aimed to pool the three institutions' complementary expertise — LSHTM's epidemiology and diagnostics, MSF's field implementation experience, and Oxford's clinical trial infrastructure — to accelerate the development and deployment of improved treatments.
MEET-024.outcome: A three-year collaborative research program was established covering five neglected tropical disease priorities. LSHTM will lead epidemiological studies and diagnostic tool validation, Oxford will conduct Phase II and III clinical trials for new treatment regimens, and MSF will implement field studies in endemic countries and provide operational feedback. A joint grant application of £8 million was submitted to the Wellcome Trust and UK FCDO. The program includes a dedicated capacity building component training 30 researchers from endemic countries.

MEET-025.title: Pandemic Preparedness Financing Emergency Session
MEET-025.purpose: Following the identification of a novel influenza strain with pandemic potential in Southeast Asia, WHO, AfDB, and the World Bank convened an emergency session to assess preparedness financing gaps and rapidly mobilize resources for containment measures. The session focused on immediate surge financing needs, coordination of technical assistance, and activation of contingency funds to support affected and at-risk countries.
MEET-025.outcome: WHO activated its Contingency Fund for Emergencies, releasing $15 million for immediate response activities. World Bank approved fast-track activation of its Pandemic Emergency Financing Facility for six at-risk countries. AfDB committed $50 million in emergency health financing for African countries along major travel corridors. A joint technical team was deployed to three countries within 48 hours to support surveillance strengthening and response planning.

MEET-026.title: HIV Treatment Access and Market Shaping Forum
MEET-026.purpose: Unitaid, IAVI, and the Gates Foundation convened to develop a comprehensive market strategy for next-generation HIV treatment and prevention products. The forum addressed the transition from injectable to long-acting antiretroviral formulations, pricing barriers for new HIV prevention modalities including broadly neutralizing antibodies, and the regulatory pathway challenges for novel HIV vaccine candidates in low-income country markets.
MEET-026.outcome: A joint market shaping strategy was adopted covering three product categories. Unitaid committed to a $120 million investment to accelerate generic manufacturing of long-acting injectable antiretrovirals, targeting a 70% price reduction within three years. IAVI agreed to include affordable access provisions in all licensing agreements for its HIV vaccine candidates. Gates Foundation committed to co-funding a regulatory harmonization initiative to streamline HIV product approvals across African regulatory agencies.

MEET-027.title: Americas Disease Surveillance Network Strengthening
MEET-027.purpose: PAHO and CDC convened to review and strengthen the Americas regional disease surveillance network, which had identified critical data gaps in real-time outbreak detection across Central America and the Caribbean. The meeting aimed to harmonize surveillance standards, expand laboratory network coverage, and integrate digital health tools including mobile-based reporting systems into the regional surveillance architecture.
MEET-027.outcome: A three-year surveillance strengthening plan was endorsed, covering expansion of PAHO's PAHO-NET laboratory network to 12 additional countries, integration of CDC's BioSense platform with PAHO's regional surveillance system, and deployment of mobile reporting tools to 5,000 community health workers across 8 priority countries. CDC committed $8 million in technical assistance and equipment. PAHO will coordinate training for 200 surveillance officers across the region.

MEET-028.title: Tuberculosis Diagnostics Access Initiative
MEET-028.purpose: Unitaid, WHO, and LSHTM convened to address the persistent gap in tuberculosis diagnostic access, where an estimated 40% of TB cases globally go undetected annually due to inadequate diagnostic infrastructure. The meeting focused on accelerating deployment of molecular diagnostic platforms, point-of-care testing tools, and AI-assisted chest X-ray interpretation in high-burden settings.
MEET-028.outcome: A TB diagnostics access roadmap was agreed, targeting detection of 90% of estimated TB cases by 2028. Unitaid committed $80 million to support procurement and market shaping for point-of-care molecular diagnostics. WHO agreed to update its TB diagnostic guidance and develop implementation support tools for national programs. LSHTM will lead an independent evaluation of AI-assisted diagnostic tools across 10 country sites.

MEET-029.title: African Health Workforce Development Training Program
MEET-029.purpose: AfDB, WHO, and Harvard University jointly organized a leadership development program for senior health ministry officials from 15 African countries. The program addressed a documented gap in health systems management capacity that was constraining effective use of external financing and implementation of national health strategies. The curriculum covered health financing management, human resources for health planning, supply chain management, and health information systems.
MEET-029.outcome: Sixty senior health officials from 15 African countries completed the two-week intensive leadership development program. A peer learning network was established among participants with quarterly virtual exchange sessions. WHO committed to providing ongoing technical mentorship to program graduates through its country offices. AfDB will prioritize program graduates as key contacts for health project implementation in their countries. Harvard agreed to develop an online version of the curriculum accessible to 500 additional health officials annually.

MEET-030.title: Malaria Vaccine Rollout Coordination Meeting
MEET-030.purpose: WHO, GAVI, PAHO, and LSHTM convened to coordinate the global rollout of the R21 malaria vaccine following WHO prequalification. The meeting addressed supply chain planning, country readiness assessments, health worker training requirements, and pharmacovigilance frameworks. PAHO's inclusion reflected plans to introduce malaria vaccines in endemic areas of Latin America for the first time.
MEET-030.outcome: A coordinated malaria vaccine introduction plan was agreed for 28 countries across sub-Saharan Africa and 6 countries in Latin America. GAVI approved funding for vaccine procurement for all 28 eligible African countries. PAHO will coordinate introduction in Latin American countries through its existing immunization infrastructure. WHO committed to developing standardized training materials and LSHTM agreed to lead post-introduction effectiveness studies across six sentinel sites.

MEET-031.title: Climate Change and Health Adaptation Planning Workshop
MEET-031.purpose: WHO, PAHO, AfDB, and Red Cross convened to develop a joint framework for health system adaptation to climate change impacts. With climate-related health burdens — including increased malaria transmission, heat-related illness, food insecurity, and extreme weather displacement — projected to cause 250,000 additional deaths annually by 2030, the meeting sought to integrate climate adaptation into health system planning and financing.
MEET-031.outcome: A joint Climate and Health Adaptation Framework was developed covering four domains: disease surveillance adaptation for climate-sensitive diseases, health infrastructure climate-proofing standards, climate-related humanitarian preparedness, and financing mechanisms for health adaptation. AfDB committed to making climate adaptation a mandatory criterion in all health sector financing from 2026. PAHO will develop regional adaptation guidance for Latin America. Red Cross will integrate climate risk assessment into all humanitarian health planning. WHO will lead development of global norms for climate-resilient health systems.

MEET-032.title: Digital Health Innovation and Data Systems Forum
MEET-032.purpose: LSHTM, Harvard, CDC, and Unitaid convened to explore the application of digital health technologies and artificial intelligence in improving health outcomes in low-resource settings. The forum examined evidence on AI-assisted diagnostics, digital therapeutics, electronic health records interoperability, and mobile health interventions, with a focus on ensuring that digital health innovations are validated, scalable, and accessible in low-income country contexts.
MEET-032.outcome: A joint digital health research agenda was agreed across four priority areas: AI-assisted diagnosis validation in low-resource settings, interoperability standards for electronic health records in fragmented health systems, mobile health behavior change interventions for chronic disease management, and digital supply chain tools for essential medicines. LSHTM and Harvard will co-lead a systematic evidence synthesis program. CDC committed to sharing its digital health surveillance tools under open-source licensing. Unitaid will fund market access studies for validated digital health tools in low-income countries.

MEET-033.title: PAHO-WHO Americas Health Emergency Response Exercise
MEET-033.purpose: PAHO and WHO conducted a joint health emergency simulation exercise for the Americas region, testing the activation and coordination of the regional emergency response framework. The exercise simulated a major earthquake affecting Central America with resulting mass casualty events, disease outbreaks, and health system disruption across three countries simultaneously.
MEET-033.outcome: The simulation successfully tested the joint incident command system between PAHO and WHO, identifying three critical gaps in inter-agency communication protocols and logistics coordination that have been addressed through updated standard operating procedures. A roster of 80 pre-certified emergency health responders was validated for rapid deployment across the Americas region. The revised emergency response framework will be formally adopted at the next PAHO Directing Council meeting.

MEET-034.title: HIV Prevention Innovation and Access Strategy
MEET-034.purpose: IAVI, Unitaid, MSF, and LSHTM convened to develop a coordinated strategy for accelerating access to next-generation HIV prevention tools including broadly neutralizing antibodies, long-acting pre-exposure prophylaxis, and HIV vaccine candidates. The meeting addressed the critical gap between promising clinical trial results and real-world access, examining regulatory, manufacturing, pricing, and health system delivery barriers.
MEET-034.outcome: A joint HIV Prevention Access Roadmap was endorsed covering regulatory acceleration strategies, manufacturing scale-up financing, and health system integration planning. IAVI committed to including access provisions in all licensing negotiations for its HIV prevention products. Unitaid approved a $60 million investment to support generic manufacturing scale-up for long-acting PrEP. MSF will conduct implementation research on delivery models for new HIV prevention tools in three high-burden countries. LSHTM will lead health economic modeling to inform pricing negotiations.

MEET-035.title: Universal Health Coverage Financing Acceleration Summit
MEET-035.purpose: AfDB, World Bank, PAHO, and WHO convened a summit to accelerate progress toward universal health coverage across Africa and Latin America, where coverage gaps remained largest. The summit focused on domestic resource mobilization, efficiency improvements in health spending, innovative financing instruments, and the role of regional development banks in co-financing UHC transitions.
MEET-035.outcome: A joint UHC Financing Acceleration Initiative was launched with a combined technical assistance package of $150 million to support 25 countries in developing and implementing credible UHC financing roadmaps. AfDB and World Bank agreed to co-finance UHC transition programs with a combined $3 billion envelope over five years. PAHO will provide technical support in Latin America and WHO globally. A UHC financing learning collaborative was established for finance and health ministries to share experiences and peer-review national plans.

MEET-F001.title: Cross-Border Payment Standards Working Group
MEET-F001.purpose: Establishing unified cross-border payment standards to reduce settlement times and transaction costs across jurisdictions.
MEET-F001.outcome: A draft cross-border payment protocol was agreed upon, targeting same-day settlement for transactions under $10,000 across participating networks.

MEET-F002.title: Regulatory Sandbox Outcomes Review
MEET-F002.purpose: Reviewing outcomes from the FCA's latest regulatory sandbox cohort and identifying best practices for scaling sandbox-tested innovations.
MEET-F002.outcome: Eight sandbox-tested innovations were approved for full market launch. FCA published updated guidance on AI-based financial advice and cryptocurrency custody requirements.

MEET-F003.title: Financial Inclusion in Emerging Markets Forum
MEET-F003.purpose: Developing strategies to accelerate financial inclusion across underbanked populations in Africa and Southeast Asia using mobile-first approaches.
MEET-F003.outcome: A joint financial inclusion roadmap targeting 100 million new users by 2027 was endorsed. M-Pesa agreed to open its API platform to partner fintechs in three additional countries.

MEET-F004.title: CBDC Technical Architecture Workshop
MEET-F004.purpose: Evaluating central bank digital currency architectures and their implications for commercial banking and payment systems.
MEET-F004.outcome: Three CBDC architecture models were assessed. BIS committed to publishing a technical framework for interoperable CBDC systems. MIT Sloan will lead economic impact modeling.

MEET-F005.title: AI in Fraud Detection Summit
MEET-F005.purpose: Sharing intelligence on AI-driven fraud detection methodologies and coordinating cross-platform fraud prevention strategies.
MEET-F005.outcome: A shared fraud intelligence database was established among participating organizations. Visa committed to open-sourcing its anomaly detection algorithm for industry use.

MEET-F006.title: Blockchain Compliance Framework Development
MEET-F006.purpose: Developing a unified compliance framework for blockchain-based financial services that satisfies regulatory requirements across major jurisdictions.
MEET-F006.outcome: A draft blockchain compliance framework covering KYC, AML, and transaction monitoring was produced for public consultation. Chainalysis provided analytical tools for framework testing.

MEET-F007.title: Open Banking API Standards Alignment
MEET-F007.purpose: Harmonizing open banking API standards across regions to enable seamless data sharing between traditional banks and fintech platforms.
MEET-F007.outcome: A common API specification for account information and payment initiation was adopted by all participants. Revolut and Stripe committed to implementation within six months.

MEET-F008.title: Digital Currency Research Symposium
MEET-F008.purpose: Presenting latest research findings on digital currency adoption patterns, monetary policy implications, and technological developments.
MEET-F008.outcome: MIT Sloan presented findings on CBDC adoption drivers. BIS shared cross-border CBDC pilot results. A joint research program on stablecoin systemic risk was launched.

MEET-F009.title: Cybersecurity Threat Intelligence Sharing Session
MEET-F009.purpose: Sharing real-time threat intelligence on cyberattacks targeting financial infrastructure and coordinating defensive responses.
MEET-F009.outcome: A real-time threat sharing protocol was established with 15-minute notification SLAs for critical threats. Joint incident response playbooks were developed for ransomware and DDoS scenarios.

MEET-F010.title: Mobile Money Interoperability Workshop
MEET-F010.purpose: Developing interoperability standards between mobile money platforms and traditional banking systems to create seamless payment corridors.
MEET-F010.outcome: An interoperability protocol enabling direct transfers between M-Pesa, Alipay, and traditional bank accounts was agreed. Pilot deployment in Kenya and Singapore scheduled for Q2 2026.

MEET-F011.title: Fintech Talent Development Program Launch
MEET-F011.purpose: Launching a cross-industry talent development program to address the critical skills gap in financial technology.
MEET-F011.outcome: A 12-month fellowship program was established placing 50 graduates in rotation across participating organizations. MIT Sloan developed the core curriculum covering AI, blockchain, and regulatory technology.

MEET-F012.title: Decentralized Finance Risk Assessment
MEET-F012.purpose: Conducting a systematic risk assessment of decentralized finance protocols and their potential impact on financial stability.
MEET-F012.outcome: A comprehensive DeFi risk taxonomy was published covering smart contract risk, liquidity risk, governance risk, and regulatory risk. Chainalysis provided on-chain data analysis for the assessment.

MEET-F013.title: Real-Time Payment Infrastructure Upgrade Planning
MEET-F013.purpose: Planning the next generation of real-time payment infrastructure capable of handling projected transaction volumes through 2030.
MEET-F013.outcome: A technology roadmap for payment infrastructure upgrades was endorsed, targeting 100,000 transactions per second capacity. Visa and JPMorgan committed to co-developing the core processing engine.

MEET-F014.title: Emerging Markets Digital Banking Strategy
MEET-F014.purpose: Developing coordinated strategies for expanding digital banking services across Africa, Southeast Asia, and Latin America.
MEET-F014.outcome: A joint market entry framework was developed for five priority countries. M-Pesa and Ant Group agreed to provide platform infrastructure for partner fintechs entering new markets.

MEET-F015.title: Crypto Asset Regulatory Harmonization Forum
MEET-F015.purpose: Working toward regulatory harmonization for crypto assets across major financial jurisdictions to reduce compliance fragmentation.
MEET-F015.outcome: A common regulatory taxonomy for crypto assets was agreed covering utility tokens, security tokens, stablecoins, and NFTs. FCA and BIS committed to advocating for adoption through international standard-setting bodies.

MEET-F016.title: AI Ethics in Financial Services Workshop
MEET-F016.purpose: Establishing ethical guidelines for AI deployment in financial services covering bias detection, explainability, and consumer protection.
MEET-F016.outcome: An AI Ethics Charter for Financial Services was signed by all participants. MIT Sloan will develop an AI audit methodology for financial institutions. FCA committed to incorporating AI ethics into supervisory assessments.

MEET-F017.title: Supply Chain Finance Innovation Lab
MEET-F017.purpose: Exploring blockchain-based supply chain finance solutions to improve working capital management for small and medium enterprises.
MEET-F017.outcome: A blockchain-based supply chain finance prototype was demonstrated, reducing invoice processing time from 30 days to 24 hours. Ant Group and JPMorgan committed to pilot deployment with 500 SMEs.

MEET-F018.title: Digital Identity and KYC Streamlining Initiative
MEET-F018.purpose: Developing a shared digital identity framework to reduce KYC duplication and improve onboarding efficiency across financial services.
MEET-F018.outcome: A federated digital identity protocol was agreed enabling verified identity portability across participating institutions. Revolut and Stripe agreed to pilot implementation. BIS endorsed the framework for central bank consideration.

MEET-F019.title: Financial Inclusion Impact Measurement Conference
MEET-F019.purpose: Developing standardized metrics for measuring the impact of financial inclusion initiatives and assessing progress toward SDG targets.
MEET-F019.outcome: A Financial Inclusion Impact Index was developed covering account ownership, transaction frequency, credit access, and savings behavior. M-Pesa provided anonymized transaction data for baseline analysis across six countries.

MEET-F020.title: Payment Security Standards Update
MEET-F020.purpose: Updating payment security standards to address emerging threats from quantum computing, deepfake fraud, and social engineering attacks.
MEET-F020.outcome: Updated payment security standards incorporating post-quantum cryptography requirements were drafted. Visa committed to implementing quantum-resistant encryption across its network by 2028.

MEET-F021.title: Neobank Regulatory Framework Consultation
MEET-F021.purpose: Consulting on an updated regulatory framework for neobanks and digital-only financial institutions addressing capital requirements, consumer protection, and operational resilience.
MEET-F021.outcome: Draft neobank regulatory guidance was produced covering capital adequacy, liquidity management, and technology governance requirements. Revolut provided operational data to inform proportionality assessments.

MEET-F022.title: Cross-Platform Tokenization Standards Workshop
MEET-F022.purpose: Developing interoperable tokenization standards for financial assets including deposits, bonds, and trade finance instruments.
MEET-F022.outcome: A common tokenization standard for financial assets was drafted, enabling cross-platform settlement. JPMorgan and Ant Group demonstrated interoperable tokenized deposit transfers between their platforms.

MEET-F023.title: Fintech Regulatory Technology Innovation Sprint
MEET-F023.purpose: Running a regulatory technology innovation sprint to develop tools that reduce compliance costs for small fintech firms.
MEET-F023.outcome: Four regtech prototypes were developed covering automated regulatory reporting, real-time transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and complaint management. FCA approved two for sandbox testing.

MEET-F024.title: Global Stablecoin Governance Framework
MEET-F024.purpose: Establishing a governance framework for global stablecoins addressing reserve management, redemption rights, and systemic risk mitigation.
MEET-F024.outcome: A stablecoin governance code of conduct was endorsed covering reserve transparency, audit requirements, and redemption guarantees. BIS committed to monitoring compliance through its existing supervisory channels.

MEET-F025.title: Agricultural Finance Digitization Program
MEET-F025.purpose: Launching a program to digitize agricultural finance in sub-Saharan Africa using mobile money platforms and satellite data for credit scoring.
MEET-F025.outcome: A $30 million agricultural finance digitization program was launched across Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda. M-Pesa will provide the payment platform, MIT Sloan will develop the credit scoring models.

MEET-F026.title: Instant Cross-Border Settlement Pilot
MEET-F026.purpose: Piloting an instant cross-border settlement system between Asian and European payment networks using distributed ledger technology.
MEET-F026.outcome: A successful pilot demonstrated 10-second cross-border settlement between Singapore and London. Visa and Ant Group processed 10,000 test transactions with 99.97% success rate.

MEET-F027.title: Embedded Finance Architecture Standards
MEET-F027.purpose: Developing technical architecture standards for embedded finance — the integration of financial services into non-financial platforms and applications.
MEET-F027.outcome: Embedded finance API standards were published covering payment initiation, lending, insurance, and investment services. Stripe presented its Banking-as-a-Service reference architecture for industry adoption.

MEET-F028.title: Financial Crime Intelligence Coordination Meeting
MEET-F028.purpose: Coordinating intelligence sharing on financial crime patterns including money laundering, sanctions evasion, and terrorist financing across digital channels.
MEET-F028.outcome: An enhanced financial crime intelligence sharing agreement was signed. Chainalysis deployed cross-chain analytics covering 15 blockchain networks. Joint investigation protocols were updated for DeFi-related financial crime.

MEET-F029.title: Digital Lending and Credit Scoring Innovation Forum
MEET-F029.purpose: Exploring AI-driven credit scoring innovations and alternative data approaches to expand access to credit for underserved populations.
MEET-F029.outcome: Guidelines for responsible AI-based credit scoring were published. Ant Group shared its experience scoring 80 million previously unbanked users. M-Pesa committed to integrating alternative credit scoring into its lending platform.

MEET-F030.title: Annual FinTech Alliance Summit 2026
MEET-F030.purpose: The annual summit bringing together all alliance members to review collective progress, set strategic priorities for 2026-2027, and strengthen cross-organizational partnerships.
MEET-F030.outcome: A comprehensive review confirmed achievement of 85% of 2025 targets. New priorities for 2026 include quantum-safe payments, AI governance, and expanding financial inclusion to 200 million additional users. Three new working groups were established.
